prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

Let me make the songs for the people, Songs for the old and young; Songs to stir like a battle-cry Wherever they are sung. Not for the clashing of sabres, For carnage nor for strife; But songs to thrill the hearts of men With more abundant life. Let me make the songs for the weary, Amid life’s fever and fret, Till hearts shall relax their tension, And careworn brows forget. Let me sing for little children, Before their footsteps stray, Sweet anthems of love and duty, To float o’er life’s highway. I would sing for the poor and aged, When shadows dim their sight; Of the bright and restful mansions, Where there shall be no night. Our world, so worn and weary, Needs music, pure and strong, To hush the jangle and discords Of sorrow, pain, and wrong. Music to soothe all its sorrow, Till war and crime shall cease; And the hearts of men grown tender Girdle the world with peace.

prompts.L5:
Please write a text about the following topic:

Keywords: Let, Songs, Wherever

outputs.L1:
Let me make songs for the people—  
Songs for the old and young;  
Songs to stir like a battle-cry  
Wherever they are sung.  

Not for the clashing of sabres,  
Nor for carnage or strife,  
But songs to thrill the hearts of men  
With more abundant life.  

Let me make songs for the weary,  
Amid life’s fever and fret,  
Until hearts relax their tension  
And careworn brows forget.  

Let me sing for little children,  
Before their footsteps stray,  
Sweet anthems of love and duty  
To float o’er life’s highway.  

I would sing for the poor and aged,  
When shadows dim their sight,  
Of the bright and restful mansions  
Where there shall be no night.  

Our world, so worn and weary,  
Needs music, pure and strong,  
To hush the jangle and discords  
Of sorrow, pain, and wrong.  

Music to soothe all its sorrow,  
Until war and crime shall cease,  
And the hearts of men, grown tender,  
Girdle the world with peace.
outputs.L2:
Let me compose music for everyone—  
for those advanced in years and for the young;  
melodies that rise with the force of a rallying call  
wherever voices carry them.

Not songs meant for the clash of swords,  
nor for bloodshed or conflict,  
but songs that awaken human hearts  
to a fuller, richer life.

Let me create songs for the tired and burdened,  
in the heat and worry of daily living,  
until anxious hearts grow calm  
and troubled faces lose their cares.

Let me sing for small children,  
before their paths wander astray,  
gentle hymns of love and responsibility  
to drift above the road of life.

I would lift my voice for the poor and the elderly,  
when darkness begins to cloud their vision,  
singing of bright, peaceful dwelling places  
where night will never fall.

This world of ours, exhausted and worn,  
needs music that is clear and powerful,  
to quiet the noise and harsh dissonance  
of grief, suffering, and injustice.

It needs music to comfort every sorrow,  
until war and wrongdoing come to an end,  
and human hearts, made gentle,  
encircle the earth with peace.
outputs.L3:
The speaker expresses a desire to create songs that can be enjoyed by people of every age, from children to the elderly. Rather than producing music that encourages violence, anger, or conflict, the speaker wants these songs to inspire energy, goodness, and a renewed love of life. The purpose of the music is not to divide people, but to uplift them and remind them of what is gentle, hopeful, and humane.

These songs are also meant to bring comfort to those who are tired or burdened by hardship. The speaker imagines music as a source of relief for weary souls and troubled hearts, offering rest from the struggles and sorrows of everyday life. Through song, people who feel weighed down by pain, worry, or disappointment might find a moment of peace and emotional healing.

The speaker is especially concerned with children. By offering them songs filled with love, kindness, and a sense of duty, the speaker hopes to guide them before they are led astray. Music becomes a moral influence, helping young people understand compassion, responsibility, and the importance of choosing the right path early in life.

The songs would also speak to the poor and the aged, giving them hope in the face of suffering, loneliness, or approaching death. For those who have endured much, the music would point toward the promise of a peaceful and eternal rest. In this way, the songs offer not only comfort in the present but also faith in a better future beyond life’s hardships.

Overall, the poem presents music as a powerful healing force. It suggests that songs can soothe sorrow, ease human suffering, reduce conflict, and bring people closer to peace. The speaker believes that music has the ability to touch hearts, calm troubled spirits, and help create a kinder and more harmonious world.
outputs.L4:
The poem is a heartfelt call to create songs that uplift and comfort all people, no matter their age, condition, or place in life. It asks for music not only for the young and joyful, but also for the old, the weary, the poor, the lonely, and those who suffer under the burdens of sorrow and hardship. Instead of answering the world’s pain with anger, violence, or conflict, the poem proposes song as a gentler and more compassionate response. It imagines music as something that can reach wounded spirits, brighten dark moments, and offer hope where despair has taken hold.

Throughout the poem, music is presented as a powerful healing force. Songs have the ability to soothe grief, calm troubled minds, and awaken kindness in hardened hearts. They can inspire people to love one another more deeply and to remember their duties to family, community, and humanity. Rather than dividing people, music can unite them; rather than deepening suffering, it can help ease it. The poem suggests that a world filled with songs of sympathy, courage, and love would be a better and more peaceful world.

Ultimately, the poem expresses faith in the moral and emotional power of art. It argues that songs can do more than entertain: they can comfort the suffering, strengthen the weak, encourage the discouraged, and guide people toward compassion. In a world troubled by pain, conflict, and despair, the poem imagines music as a force that can soften human hearts and help bring peace.
outputs.L5:
Let songs follow you wherever you go.

In quiet mornings, they can lift your spirit before the day begins. On long roads, they can turn the distance into a memory. In moments of sadness, songs can speak the words you cannot find. Wherever life takes you—through joy, change, hope, or uncertainty—music has a way of staying close.

Let each song become a small companion, reminding you of who you are, where you have been, and what you still dream of becoming. Some songs bring comfort, some bring courage, and some simply make the world feel a little brighter.

So wherever you are, let songs be part of the journey.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write an uplifting, old-fashioned poem about making songs for all people—children, the weary, the poor, and the aged—that promotes peace, comfort, love, and moral duty.
counterfactuals.output:
**Songs for All**

I would make songs for the little child,  
With laughter like the morn,  
Of daisied fields and running brooks,  
And hope but newly born;  
That every heart, so small and fair,  
May learn, while yet it sings,  
To love the world, and speak the truth,  
And trust the King of kings.

I would make songs for the weary ones,  
Who labor through the day,  
Whose hands are worn with honest toil,  
Whose skies are often gray;  
A song to bid their burdens light,  
Their patient spirits rise,  
And tell them peace is near at hand  
Beneath the evening skies.

I would make songs for the poor and lone,  
Who sit beside the door,  
And count the scanty loaf with care,  
And wish that it were more;  
A song of bread for every soul,  
Of kindness freely given,  
For he who shares his crust on earth  
Has laid up gold in heaven.

I would make songs for the aged feet  
That falter on the way,  
For silver hair and tender eyes  
That dream of yesterday;  
A song to soothe the twilight hour,  
To make the shadows cease,  
And whisper, “After faithful toil,  
The Lord shall grant thee peace.”

I would make songs for all mankind,  
For palace, cot, and street,  
That hearts long sundered by their pride  
Might in forgiveness meet;  
No bitter word, no cruel hand,  
No sword, no wrathful flame—  
But love to guide the nations on,  
And duty’s holy name.

So let the song go round the earth,  
As winds through orchards blow,  
Till every child and weary soul  
Its blessed tune shall know;  
And may it teach, from shore to shore,  
Wherever men may roam:  
Peace is the road, and love the light,  
And duty leads us home.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Compose a hymn-like inspirational poem in a 19th-century style beginning with “Let me make the songs for the people,” focusing on music as a force for healing the world.
counterfactuals.output:
Let me make the songs for the people,  
Songs for the weary and worn,  
Strains that shall rise like a steeple  
Into the light of the morn;  
Notes that shall gather the grieving,  
Chords that shall strengthen the weak,  
Music of hope and believing,  
Mercy the lowly may speak.

Let me make hymns for the nations,  
Anthems of brotherly grace,  
Till from their dark habitations  
Hatred shall vanish its face;  
Till, where the war-drum was sounding,  
Children in safety shall sing,  
And, where the sorrow was wounding,  
Peace shall spread wide like the spring.

Give me the harp of compassion,  
Give me the trumpet of truth;  
Let not the world’s weary passion  
Silence the gladness of youth.  
Over the prison and hovel,  
Over the palace and mart,  
Let the bright measures of love all  
Enter and soften the heart.

Music shall bind up the broken,  
Music shall comfort the slain;  
Words that in kindness are spoken  
Rise like the fields after rain.  
Out of the night and its weeping,  
Out of the tumult and wrong,  
Souls shall awaken from sleeping,  
Led by the lamp of a song.

Then let the choirs be assembled,  
High over mountain and sea;  
Let every proud heart be humbled,  
Let every captive be free.  
Earth shall remember her calling,  
Heaven shall answer above,  
When, through the ages enthralling,  
Music is married to love.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a sentimental poem about the power of songs to soothe sorrow, inspire abundant life, guide children, comfort the elderly, and bring peace instead of war.
counterfactuals.output:
**The Song That Holds Us**

When sorrow sits beside the bed  
and shadows crowd the wall,  
a gentle song can lift its head  
and answer to the call.  

It does not mend the world at once  
or make all grieving cease,  
but wraps the heart in tender warmth  
and teaches it of peace.  

A song can wake the sleeping field  
and bid the blossoms rise,  
can turn a cup of simple rain  
to rivers in our eyes.  
It plants bright seeds in weary souls,  
where hope had thinned like air,  
and makes an abundant life grow green  
from love, and breath, and prayer.  

For children, songs are little lamps  
that shine along the way,  
they teach the names of stars and streams,  
of kindness, work, and play.  
They hold small hands through fear and night,  
through first goodbyes and tears,  
and sing them toward a braver dawn  
across the bridge of years.  

For those grown old, a song returns  
like footsteps at the door,  
bringing back the vanished rooms  
and voices heard before.  
It rocks the tired heart to rest,  
it softens time’s decree,  
and lets the silvered spirit drift  
on memory’s gentle sea.  

O let us sing instead of strike,  
let drums of war be still;  
let every anthem choose the seed  
over the sword and hill.  
For music knows what anger forgets:  
all hearts were made to ache,  
and every note that joins our breath  
is one less wall we make.  

So sing when sorrow finds you,  
sing when joy is near;  
sing for the child just starting out,  
the elder drawing near.  
Sing till the wounded world remembers  
what it was living for—  
a lullaby, a harvest hymn,  
and peace instead of war.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Please write a public-domain-style religious/moral verse about singing for humanity, with themes of weariness, care, children, heaven, and ending violence through music.
counterfactuals.output:
When hearts are worn with grief and care,  
And weary feet have lost the way,  
Let one clear song arise like prayer  
To turn the night toward day.

Sing for the child with tearful eyes,  
For hands that hunger, homes that fall;  
Let mercy’s music climb the skies  
And heaven bend over all.

No sword shall rule where voices blend,  
No wrath endure where love is strong;  
O God, make every foe a friend,  
And end all war with song.

Then let us sing for humankind,  
Till fear and cruelty cease to be;  
Till every burdened soul shall find  
Peace, hope, and charity.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Create a rhyming poem in formal language where the speaker asks to make songs not for battle or strife, but to uplift hearts and help the world grow peaceful.
counterfactuals.output:
Make songs, I pray, not forged for war,  
Nor tuned to wrath’s resounding cry;  
Let no fierce drum from shore to shore  
Command the wounded world to die.  

But weave such notes as hearts may raise,  
When sorrow bends beneath its load;  
Let kindness kindle in their praise,  
And light the dark and stony road.  

Sing not of banners steeped in flame,  
Nor laurels won through grief and pain;  
Let mercy be the nobler name,  
And concord be the sweeter gain.  

Make songs that bid all hatred cease,  
That teach the restless soul to mend;  
So may the earth grow green with peace,  
And stranger greet each stranger—friend.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
